title: literalSet reads x+ as x, so a regex matcher with an unbounded repetition is rewritten to a finite IN set
notes: Adds syntax.OpPlus to the OpCapture arm of literalSet (internal/chsql/regex_literal_set.go), so `x+` is read as the language of `x` alone. anchoredRegexLiteralSet then accepts a pattern whose language is infinite: job=~"a+" is rewritten to job = 'a', and job=~"\\d+" to job IN ('0', …, '9'). The rewritten matcher no longer answers what match() over the anchored pattern ^(?:a+)$ answers: it rejects "aa" where match() accepts it, and the negated matcher keeps "aa" where NOT match() drops it. The rewrite is the second of the two SQL forms a chplan.OpMatch/OpNotMatch label matcher renders through (Builder.regexMatcher in internal/chsql/builder.go), and it is shared by every head, so the mutation breaks PromQL and LogQL matchers alike. The detector, TestRegexLiteralSet_AnswersAsAnchoredMatch_ChDB, renders each pattern of its corpus both ways — through the production Builder path and through anchoredRegexMatch, the match() form the rewrite replaces — executes both for =~ and !~ against one chDB table, and fails on every row where they differ. The table holds the absent label, the empty value, invalid UTF-8 and the near misses of every member, both of the hand-written member lists the test carries and of the sets the rewrite returns; the near misses include the member repeated, which is the value this mutation gets wrong. The kill is an answer divergence on chDB, not a shape assertion: the detector asserts only that the patterns it marks rewritten are rewritten, never that the others are not. It needs the chdb build tag and libchdb.so.
